messages:
tess: Heads-up — seeing 3 OOMs on gpu-pool-4 during the 08:12 canary window. All of them correlate with the kernel_selector choosing matmul_fallback + large batch window.

sam: ugh. any stack snippets? is it allocator fragmentation or just workspace sizing?

(tess pasted logs)

`tess:
[08:12:04] kernel_selector: chosen=matmul_fallback (latency_est=12ms, mem_est=1.9GiB)
[08:12:05] batcher: window=128, queued=95
[08:12:05] kv_cache: hit_rate=0.62, kv_mem=1.1GiB
[08:12:06] allocator: allocate failed size=512MiB err=CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
[08:12:06] runtime: evict_policy=soft (0 evictions)
`

dinesh: looks like two compounding issues: (1) batcher window expanded during tail of workload -> big allocations at once, (2) kernel_selector picked fallback with worse workspace footprint. kv_cache using 1.1GiB leaves less headroom.

sam: agree. we should patch in order: reduce max_batch_window for pool-4, bias kernel_selector toward low-memory kernels under pressure, and enable opportunistic KV eviction threshold.

ops-oncall: what's the quick mitigation we can push now? customer impact is <5% but rising.

tess: quick mitigation plan I propose:
- Enable soft-circuit at 80% GPU mem used -> force routing to small-model-variants and reduce batch window to 32.
- Set kernel_selector memory_penalty:+0.25 for fallback kernels (bias to smaller workspaces).
- Turn on kv_cache.auto_trim at 0.5 to free ~500MiB.

Config I'll push to canary (pool-4 only):
```yaml
canary_patch:
  target_pools: ["gpu-pool-4"]
  actions:
    - set: batcher.max_window
      value: 32
    - set: kernel_selector.memory_penalty.matmul_fallback
      value: 0.25
    - set: kv_cache.auto_trim_threshold
      value: 0.5
    - set: circuit.soft_threshold
      value: 0.8
    - set: routing.fallback_models
      value: ["small-variant-v1"]
```

infra-bot: deploy triggered: canary_patch -> gpu-pool-4 (id: cp-2026-09-12-08-28). CI checks passed.

sam: monitor metrics: OOM_count, allocator.fail_rate, avg_batch_size, kv_mem, selected_kernel_distribution. Add a temporary alert if OOM_count > 1 in 5m.

dinesh: longer term items to avoid recurrence:
- Add kernel selection cost model that includes peak_workspace instead of only flops/latency estimates.
- Opportunistic buffer reuse across sequential requests when KV cache hit implies same prefix. (should reclaim workspace for next request)
- Batcher: make dynamic window shrink when allocator fragmentation rises (measure free_chunks < threshold).

ops-oncall: ok pushing canary now. If OOMs cease, promote in 30m. If still see OOMs, fallback plan: full pool-level circuit to route live traffic to dedicated-fallback fleet and throttle writes to KV cache.

tess: canary deployed. linking perf dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/gpu-pool-4/canary-cp-2026-09-12-08-28

infra-bot: metric snapshot at deploy: {OOM_count:0, avg_batch:78, kv_mem:1.12GiB, gpu_util:67%}

(30m later)

ops-oncall: quick update — OOMs dropped to 0 in last 10m, avg_batch reduced to 31, selected_kernel_distribution shifted: matmul_fallback 12% -> 3%. kv_mem trimmed ~430MiB. Looks good. :thumbsup:

sam: great. follow-ups: open PR for kernel_selector cost model, ticket for buffer-reuse prototype, and adjust canary to progressively increase batch window if signals stay green.

dinesh: I'll take the buffer-reuse prototype. tagging infra to help with docs for the soft-circuit behavior.

tess: thanks everyone. I logged postmortem draft and action items: https://go/reports/oom-canary-2026-09-12 (will fill root cause and timeline).

infra-bot: ticket created: RNDR-3421 (kernel_cost_model).

sam: closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions show up.
